quotes.text: VPNs trust the network, not the user. They check your credentials at the door, and then assume everything is fine for the rest of the session. That's the opposite of what modern security needs.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints the core weakness of the traditional VPN model.

quotes.text: Instead of protecting a network, you're protecting identities. Instead of building walls, you're building policies. And instead of trusting a connection, you're verifying every request.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the shift from network trust to identity trust in three contrasts.

quotes.text: If you have a conditional access policy requiring the global secure access client, that stolen token is useless. The attacker's device doesn't have the client installed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains concretely how the compliant network check defeats token theft.

quotes.text: The simplest starting point is a policy that requires the Global Secure Access client for all Cloud app access. That single policy blocks token theft attacks and gives you immediate value.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete, low-effort first step admins can take right away.

chapters.title: From network trust to identity trust

takeaways: Traditional VPNs trust the network and grant broad access, while Microsoft Entra Internet Access verifies identity, device and risk for every request.
Global Secure Access routes traffic through Microsoft, internet and private access profiles, and Conditional Access can require the client to block stolen-token attacks.
Web content filtering, TLS inspection, tenant restrictions and shadow AI discovery run at the network level, and the Microsoft traffic profile is already included with Entra ID P1.
hook: VPNs give remote users far too much access and create constant help desk friction. This Simply Explained episode is for IT admins and security teams who want to understand how Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Global Secure Access replace network trust with identity-driven Zero Trust, how Conditional Access stops token theft and how to get started with licensing.
